newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit slips back on dollar/majors strength.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit slips back on dollar/majors strength.

text.p: The ringgit fell back against the dollar in late Asian trading on Wednesday following the dollar's strength against major currencies, dealers said.

"Dollar bids came out again on the back of dollar's firmness against majors, particularly against the yen," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. He said the ringgit's fall also reflected a retreat in other regional currencies against the dollar.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6250/80 to a dollar, after hitting a high of 2.6210 in the morning.
Dollar/ringgit might test higher levels during London trading, the dealer said.

Dealers said the initial ringgit firmness was aided by unconfirmed talk that the U.S. authorities were asking hedge funds to unwind from long dollar/regionals positions, and Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's continued verbal attack on currency speculators.

Local newspapers quoted Mahathir as saying Malaysians became involved in the recent attacks on the ringgit by making the currency available to speculators and may also have been seeking profit themselves.
"The market feels that if he continues to talk this way there may be some action down the line. So people are wary," said an analyst with a research firm in Singapore.
Dealers said Mahathir's remarks were prompting Kuala Lumpur corporates and exporters to sell the dollar on any rallies.
